findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a well-known Python dataclass pitfall: `timezone.now()` is called once when the class body executes (at module import), not each time an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. Every instance created without an explicit `queued` will share the same import-time timestamp, so `queued` no longer represents "when this assignment source was queued". Fix by importing `field` from `dataclasses` and writing `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The current test only asserts `queued is not None`, which masks the bug. The field is not yet consumed by any logic, but it is part of the persisted payload and any future use for TTL, deduplication, or staleness checks will be wrong.

findings.title: Test name typo: `inalid_data`
findings.body: Test method `test_from_dict_inalid_data` has a typo (`inalid` instead of `invalid`). The name shows up in test runner output and failure messages, making the suite harder to read and conflating a misspelling with a real bug during triage.

findings.title: Test name `test_from_dict_empty_array` actually exercises an empty dict
findings.body: The test is named `test_from_dict_empty_array` but passes `data: dict[str, Any] = {}` (an empty dict). If the intent is to assert behavior on an empty mapping, the name should reflect that; otherwise readers will look for an empty-list case that does not exist. This is the kind of misleading test name that causes future contributors to add a second, redundant test for the wrong shape.
